input.subject: Just checking in, no rush
input.body: Hi Nia, not chasing, just curious how the book is going. I have been quiet on the updates because I figured you would post when there was something to post. Hope the printing is going well.

engine.draftText:
Hi Bram,

Thanks for checking in — and for being so patient. It’s been 68 days now, and I know that’s a long stretch to wait without much to see.

Right now the books are in binding and check. That means all the signatures are folded and sewn, and I’m going through a sample from every stack to make sure the offset and registration are where they need to be. It’s the kind of slow, careful work that doesn’t make for a great photo, but it’s what keeps the pages lining up the way they should.

From here, the books will move to the fulfilment room, then to packing and posting. I’m looking at ships in weeks 2–4.

I’ll post again when there’s a real shift to share. Thanks again for the quiet trust.

- Nia, Foldwork Press

input.subject: Shipping to Canada?
input.body: Is Canada in the same shipping wave as the US or do we go later? Last campaign I backed, we went two months later and nobody said so up front.

engine.draftText:
Marcus,

Thank you for writing in. I can see you've been waiting 94 days, and I know that kind of wait can feel uncertain, especially when you've been burned by a campaign before. I want to be straightforward with you about where things stand.

Right now we're past the paper stage — the uncoated stock for the interior is ordered and the cover board is confirmed with the mill. That part is done. The books are moving through the press runs, one colour at a time, and each pass has to dry before the next one. It's the slowest part of the process, but it's the part that makes the final book look the way it should.

As for shipping waves: I pack everything by hand in pledge order, oldest first, regardless of country. Canada and US orders are packed together in that same sequence. I don't split by region. So your place in line is the same as anyone else's.

The books will ship in weeks 4–6 from now. I don't have a calendar date to give you, but that's the window I'm working toward.

- Nia, Foldwork Press

input.subject: Was I charged twice?
input.body: I see two charges from Kickstarter on my card. Did something go wrong with my pledge?

engine.draftText:
Ivy,

I hear you — seeing two charges is unsettling, especially when you’ve already been waiting 81 days. Let me walk through what’s happening on my end.

Right now your book is in the binding and check stage. The signatures are folded and sewn, and I’m going through a sample from every stack to make sure the offset and registration are clean. It’s the kind of slow checking that keeps the books right, but it means I’m not in the payment system today.

If you saw two charges from Kickstarter, that’s something only Kickstarter’s billing team can sort out — I don’t process payments on my side. The best thing is to reach out to Kickstarter support directly and ask them to look at your pledge history. They’ll be able to see if it was a duplicate authorization or a hold that fell off.

Your book ships in weeks 1–2, and I’ll send a note the moment yours is handed to the post office.

- Nia, Foldwork Press

input.subject: Add a second copy?
input.body: Can I add another copy for a friend and pay you directly? I do not want to miss the run.

engine.draftText:
Hey Owen,

Thanks for reaching out. I can see you’ve been waiting 76 days now, and I appreciate your patience through this long print stage. Right now the books are on press — the Risograph runs one colour at a time, and each pass has to dry before the next one, which is why this stage is the long one. It’s slow, but it’s how the colours stay crisp.

I’m not set up to take direct payments for extra copies outside the crowdfunding system, so I wouldn’t want you to miss the run either. The best way to add a second copy is to check if the campaign page still has an add-on option open. input.subject: EU wave
input.body: I am in Germany. Are the EU pallets on the same boat as the US ones or not? The last campaign I backed shipped the US in March and the EU in July and never said a word about it in advance.

engine.draftText:
Hi Dana,

I understand the concern—waiting 70 days without a clear picture can feel like a lot, especially when you've had a rough experience with another campaign's EU shipping. Let me lay out exactly how we handle it.

The EU and US containers sail on different weeks and clear customs at different speeds. They're separate from the start, so there's no single boat carrying both. That's why the two waves separate during the sea freight stage, and why EU backers sometimes see their pledges move at a different pace than US backers.

Right now we're in the casting stage, which runs in SKU order, not backer order. If your pledge includes a late-sculpted expansion, it waits for that expansion's moulds and casting to finish. That's the main variable for how long a given pledge takes to move through this stage.

For your specific situation, the timing we're working with is "ships in weeks 1–4." That's the window we're aiming for from here, but it's a range, not a fixed date—because casting, sprue checks, and customs all have their own rhythms.

I know that's not a calendar date, and I wish I could give you one. But I'd rather be straightforward about how the process actually works than promise something that might shift. You're not forgotten, and your pledge is moving through the system.

- Teodora, Brasslight

input.subject: SKU order
input.body: I have the base game plus four expansions. Does that make me later than someone with just the base game?

engine.draftText:
Hey Owen,

Great question. Yes, that’s exactly how it works. Casting runs in SKU order, not backer order, so a pledge with multiple expansions—especially ones that were sculpted later—gets queued behind simpler base-game-only orders. Each expansion has its own mould, and those moulds are made after the core set’s are locked, so they take longer to get through casting.

Right now we’re in the sprue check stage. That means we pull a sample from each lot and inspect for short shots and flash. If a lot fails, it gets recast, which slows the whole SKU. Your pledge includes four expansions, so it’s likely in a later lot than a base-game-only pledge.

All that said, your order ships in weeks 1–3. We’re moving through the checks as fast as the moulds and lots allow.

- Teodora, Brasslight

merchantEvents.body: Gorgias HTTP integration pointed at the Tideover ingest endpoint with an Authorization: Bearer header.
merchantEvents.expectedOperatorAction: BLOCKER, surface it now: Gorgias can only attach a static header or OAuth2. It cannot compute a per-request HMAC, so it cannot produce X-Tideover-Signature. The instant DEMO_MODE goes false, every ticket 401s. Second check: send one test ticket and confirm the body is not empty - CanonicalIngestSchema has no .min(1) on body, so an unrendered placeholder ingests silently as empty, classifies as 'other'/'calm', and buries anything urgent at the bottom of the queue.

merchantEvents.subject: Correcting the shipping email
merchantEvents.body: Broadcast to every open preorder: the confirmation email you received quoted a 3-5 day window. That was wrong. The real band is 90-110 days from order, which is what the product page says.
merchantEvents.expectedOperatorAction: Send it before the wave hits, not after. Include the status link in the correction. A wrong hard date fires a support avalanche across the whole list at once - this is the clearest live proof for the hard-date-free doctrine in the whole product.

merchantEvents.subject: Help Scout will not connect - forwarding instead
merchantEvents.body: Attempted the standard webhook setup. Help Scout's payload is fixed and signs with base64(HMAC-SHA1) under X-HelpScout-Signature. Tideover wants templated canonical JSON and sha256 hex under X-Tideover-Signature.
merchantEvents.expectedOperatorAction: SURFACE THIS, do not work around it quietly. The canonical ingest rail cannot accept Help Scout at all; a real integration is a net-new vendor adapter plus a normalizer plus a second signature scheme. For this sim, set up email forwarding into the inbound address and expect the identity problem below. Also note Help Scout tags are objects, not strings - any tag filter written for the string rail misreads them.

merchantEvents.subject: Second colour sample rejected
merchantEvents.body: Broadcast: we rejected the second resin sample - the alpha was off by enough to matter. Third sample is running. Band widens by about two weeks and I would rather do that than ship you a bad colour.
merchantEvents.expectedOperatorAction: Widen the band. Post the sample photos. In this community, showing the rejected sample buys more goodwill than any apology copy could - so let the photo do the work and keep the copy short.

input.subject: Deepwater - freight?
input.body: Backed Deepwater in the spring. Where is the container? And I notice you had time to launch a new campaign.

engine.draftText:
Dana,

You’re right to be frustrated — 101 days is a long wait, and I’m sorry we haven’t made the process feel more visible. The Deepwater containers are in sea freight now, heading to the regional hubs. Those hubs receive on different weeks and clear customs at different speeds, so there’s a range rather than a single date. What we can say is that yours ships in weeks 4–6.

And yes, we did launch another campaign. I know that stings when you’re still waiting. We’re a two-person studio, and the reality is that running a crowdfunding business means we have to keep the next project moving to stay afloat — but I also know that doesn’t make the wait for Deepwater any easier. We’re not pretending the two aren’t connected, and we’re not happy about the gap either.

Thank you for sticking with us through this.

- Jamie, Two Lantern

input.subject: Saltmarsh - should I be worried?
input.body: I just backed Saltmarsh. Then I read the Deepwater comments. Should I be pulling my pledge?

engine.draftText:
Hey Dana,

Thanks for reaching out, and I hear the worry in your message. You're right to notice that we're running two campaigns, and I won't pretend they're unrelated—they're both ours, and we're learning as we go. Deepwater's had its bumps, and we've been open about that. But Saltmarsh is a different project, and we're in a different place with it.

Right now, Saltmarsh is in the components-sourced stage: cardstock, wood tokens, and the miniatures resin are locked with the manufacturer. That's the first of several steps, and we're working through them one at a time. You've been waiting 6 days, which is early days for a preorder like this. Based on where we are, your copy ships in weeks 3–5.

I know waiting is uncomfortable, especially when you've seen other projects hit snags. We're not going to pretend there's zero risk—crowdfunding always has some—but we're focused on getting this one right, not fast. If you decide to pull your pledge, we'll understand. But if you stay, we'll keep you posted with the same candor we've used here.

- Jamie, Two Lantern

input.subject: I am in both
input.body: I backed Deepwater and Saltmarsh. Can you ship them together and save me the shipping?

engine.draftText:
Hey Mika,

Thanks for reaching out. I see you're in on both campaigns, and I get the appeal of combining them—it makes sense.

Here's the thing: Deepwater and Saltmarsh are on different production tracks, and they're not synced up timing-wise. Deepwater is further along, while Saltmarsh is still in pre-production copy—we're playing through our one full copy right now, checking every component against the manifest before we release the run. That means Saltmarsh ships in weeks 1–3.

If we held Deepwater to wait for Saltmarsh, you'd be waiting longer for the one that's ready sooner. And if we shipped them together, we'd have to adjust the logistics on our end in a way that doesn't really save you anything—the shipping cost is based on weight and destination, not how many boxes we send.

I know that's not the answer you were hoping for, and I'm sorry for the awkwardness of having two campaigns that don't line up neatly. We're a two-person studio, and we're learning as we go. Thanks for sticking with us through it.

- Jamie, Two Lantern

input.subject: Saltmarsh timeline
input.body: What is the actual production timeline for Saltmarsh? And be more careful with it than you were with Deepwater.

engine.draftText:
Hey Owen,

Thanks for checking in, and I hear the frustration — 13 days is a long time to sit with a preorder, especially when you’ve been through a campaign before. You’re right to ask for specifics, and I want to be straight with you about where Saltmarsh actually is.

Right now we’re in the first stage: components sourced. That means the cardstock, wood tokens, and miniatures resin are all locked with the manufacturer. Nothing’s in limbo. The next step is manufacturing — printing, punching, and moulding — which is the longest stretch and the one most likely to shift. After that comes pre-production copy, then sea freight, then hub dispatch.

The timeline we’re working from is that Saltmarsh ships in weeks 2–4. That’s the confidence band we have today. I won’t pretend it’s tighter than it is, and I won’t give you a date that could slip. What I can say is we’re not guessing — we’re watching each stage as it happens, and I’ll update you the moment anything changes.

I know that’s not the same as having it in hand. But I’d rather give you a real window than a false one.

- Jamie, Two Lantern

engine.draftText:
Mika,

You're right to call this out, and I appreciate you saying it directly. We've been sitting on your question about combining the two orders, and that's on us — we should have answered sooner, even if the answer wasn't what you wanted.

The second campaign is further behind, so combining them would mean holding the first until the second catches up, which would push your first order past its current window. We can do that if you prefer, but we wanted to lay out the trade-off clearly.

As for timing on the first campaign: it ships in weeks 5–8. That's the best estimate we have right now, and we'll update you the moment we have anything more specific.

We know 104 days is a long wait, and we don't take that lightly. We're a two-person studio, and every delay stings for us too — we're not pretending these campaigns are unrelated. If you want to combine, just say the word and we'll adjust your fulfillment. If you'd rather keep them separate, we'll get the first one out as soon as it's ready.

- Jamie, Two Lantern

input.subject: VIP: the review channel
input.body: This is the board game channel that covered Deepwater. We are being asked in our comments why we recommended it. What do we tell them?

engine.draftText:
Sasha,

Thanks for writing in, and I hear the anxiety. 119 days is a long time to wait, and I know that can feel like a lot of silence on our end. Let me lay out exactly where we are.

Your copy is currently in sea freight — that’s the stage where containers are moving to regional hubs. Those hubs receive on different weeks and clear customs at different speeds, which is the part we can’t control or predict with any precision. What I can tell you is that your copy ships in weeks 1–4 from now. That’s the band we’re working inside.

We don’t pretend the two campaigns are unrelated. The wait for Deepwater has been longer than we wanted, and we’ve been candid about the manufacturing and shipping timeline shifting. We’re not going to tell you it’s been smooth — it hasn’t. But we are in the final stretch, and every container that clears is one step closer to your doorstep.

If the review channel wants to know what to tell their audience, the honest (and I know we don’t use that word lightly) answer is: the game is real, the production is done, and it’s on the water. We’re shipping as fast as the logistics chain allows.

- Jamie, Two Lantern

input.subject: My referral shipped before me
input.body: My referral ordered four days after I did and his machine has shipped. Mine has not. Same configuration. What is the ordering logic here, because from where I sit there is not one.

engine.draftText:
Owen,

I can see why that looks wrong. The dispatch stage runs in block order, which is set by your order date — oldest first. If your referral ordered four days after you, his block number should be later than yours. What likely happened is that his block finished calibration and cut test ahead of yours, and a block never ships whole because machines that miss tolerance go back to the bench. That means some blocks ship in pieces, and earlier blocks can appear to trail later ones when a unit needs rework.

Your order has been waiting 347 days. We are running a little longer than planned — see the update below. The current stage is Dispatch, out of your regional warehouse, in block order. Your block number is on your status page.

- Odette, Foundry One

Your block number is set by your order date, oldest first. That has not changed.

The only timing I can give you is that your unit ships in weeks 1–4. I cannot give you a calendar date because the last two were wrong, and I will not repeat that mistake.

- Odette, Foundry One

merchantEvents.subject: 9,000 preorders, day 140, six-month slip announced last month
merchantEvents.body: CSV export from Shopify (no API wiring). Gorgias connected. Average order $799.
merchantEvents.expectedOperatorAction: Three checks before the queue is trusted. (1) The Gorgias signature problem: no per-request HMAC exists, so every ticket 401s once DEMO_MODE is false. (2) The empty-body hole: send a test ticket and confirm the body renders, or a chargeback threat sorts to the bottom as 'other/calm'. (3) The LTV tier fires for all 9,000 at $799 vs a $500 threshold, so it is not a discriminator here - priority has to come from the refund-risk band alone.

merchantEvents.subject: Enclosure tooling: what actually happened
merchantEvents.body: Broadcast: the sheet-metal tool failed final validation twice. We have moved to a second tooling vendor. Band moves to 150-240 days from order. We are not issuing a new hard date, because the last two we issued were wrong and that is worse than saying we do not know.
merchantEvents.expectedOperatorAction: Widen the band, publish the tooling report, push status links to every block. Refuse to issue a date - the customer word in the tickets is already 'lies', which is what a slipped hard date becomes. Then staff the next 10 days for the wave: expect the WISMO forecast to spike and refund requests to follow 48-72 hours behind.

update.text: Broadcast: the sheet-metal tool failed final validation twice. We have moved to a second tooling vendor. Band moves to 150-240 days from order. We are not issuing a new hard date, because the last two we issued were wrong and that is worse than saying we do not know.

merchantEvents.subject: Community forum: 400 posts in 24 hours
merchantEvents.body: Forum spike after the announcement. 'Seriously. This is pathetic. Another push back. I gave you kind views on every previous delay and this is over the top now.' Second thread is people comparing refund-request response times.
merchantEvents.expectedOperatorAction: Goodwill from previous delays is spent and cannot be recharged with words. Post once, in public, with the tooling report attached. Then let the status page carry the weight - one-to-one replies to 400 posts is not a strategy, it is a way to lose a week.
merchantEvents.note: NO product surface. A public comment wall (Kickstarter/Gamefound/BackerKit/Discord) cannot be ingested, triaged, drafted for, or answered. Tideover is inbox-only.

merchantEvents.subject: 30-day outcome review
merchantEvents.body: Operator reviews the ledger: refunds requested, refunds prevented, disputes filed, reply-time distribution.
merchantEvents.expectedOperatorAction: Report from the ledger only. Any refunds-prevented or hours-saved figure must be shown as a formula with its assumptions (tickets x AHT, or requests x save-rate) and labelled SIMULATED. Do not assert a measured result from a simulated run.

adapter.note: Values the harness DERIVED from the approved persona (everything else is read verbatim). Recorded so no output number is unattributable.
adapter.disclosedEta: OMITTED — no export in this market carries a delivery-date column (persona.dataReceived)

apiFriction.where: lib/service.ts:447 ingestTicket (and :186 intelToDraft, :522 drafter.draft, :531 computeTicketIntelligence), lib/gift-send.ts:47
apiFriction.what: The ENGINES all take an injectable `now`, but the SERVICE layer never passes one: ingestTicket's options are only { draftTimeoutMs }, and it calls computeTicketIntelligence / drafter.draft / intelToDraft with no date. authorizeGiftSend calls computeTimeline(order, merchant) with no now. Result: you cannot ingest a ticket 'as of day 12' — the whole ingest path reads the wall clock. This blocks backfill/replay, time-travel QA, and any deterministic end-to-end test of the wait math.
apiFriction.workaround: The harness monkeypatches global Date so every internal new Date()/Date.now() resolves to the sim instant.

apiFriction.what: importBackerRows() takes a `now` (lib/import.ts:104) but the onboarding call site omits it, so the atomic wizard import always anchors initial production-stage derivation to wall-clock now.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness moves the global clock instead of passing a date.

apiFriction.what: Onboarding never creates ScriptVariants, so a real merchant's sends resolve no variantId; recordReplySent() returns null and writes NO reply_sent event. Outcome ledger, Script Performance, CSAT attribution, reopen + quiet-resolution rates and the promote-variant flow are all silently dead for every non-demo merchant.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness seeds 4 day-stage base variants from merchant.playbook via repos.scriptVariants.create.

apiFriction.what: ingestTicket computes ticketsLast7d BEFORE creating the ticket, so the riskScore stamped on DraftReply excludes the ticket itself; getTicketView/getQueue recompute it AFTER, including it. The persisted draft.riskScore therefore never equals the score the cockpit shows for the same ticket (observed: 40 vs 44, 62 vs 66 — a fixed +4 repeat-contact factor). Anything reading draft.riskScore (evidence pack, exports) disagrees with the UI.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness records BOTH numbers per event (riskScoreAtIngest, riskScoreInCockpit).

apiFriction.what: Posting a workshop update writes a row and nothing else. There is no push to the cohort: no email, no status-link send, no notification. The update only exists for a customer who independently returns to their status page. Every persona's playbook is 'announce, then push the status link to the cohort' — the second half does not exist.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness records the post; no delivery is attempted because none is possible.

apiFriction.what: The pile-on — 40 to 300+ PUBLIC comments in hours after a delay post — is the single loudest moment in every persona, and the product cannot see it. Every adapter is a 1:1 private-ticket channel; a Ticket belongs to one customer and one order. There is no many-to-one public thread, no 'reply once in public', no way to measure or deflect the wall. The merchant's worst hour is invisible to the tool they bought to survive it.
apiFriction.workaround: Recorded as an unrepresentable event; no ticket is created.

apiFriction.where: lib/evidence.ts assembleEvidencePack + lib/csv.ts (no delivery-date column exists to import)
apiFriction.what: On a live chargeback threat the evidence pack assembles with NO disclosed ETA and no disclosure timestamp — for EVERY persona, because no export in this market (KS backer report, KS pledge manager, BackerKit, Gamefound, Shopify CSV) carries a delivery-date column. 'We told you X on date Y, and you accepted it' is the strongest exhibit in a card-network rebuttal, and the pack cannot produce it for anyone. Every order also lands in disputeExposure.unknownCount, so the dashboard tile reads 100% unknown across all 10 merchants.
apiFriction.workaround: None available. The operator would have to type the disclosed band by hand per order; there is no field and no bulk path.

apiFriction.what: CSAT attribution (find the order's last reply_sent, replace prior tap, record csat_up/down) is implemented in the route handler, not the service layer — unreachable from any non-HTTP caller and untestable without fabricating a Request.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness constructs a Request and invokes the route's POST export directly.

apiFriction.what: A delay that hits ONE cohort (here: late-pledge) cannot be expressed. The band is a single merchant-wide { min, max } and a workshop update is a single merchant-wide text. So widening for the EU container ALSO widens the US backers' band and posts the EU delay to everyone — the exact 'panic in the cohort that was not affected' the personas describe. There is no campaign, wave, region or segment to scope either one to.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness moves the merchant-wide band and posts one merchant-wide update.

apiFriction.where: lib/ingest-route.ts (drop-at-edge) → no counter, no dead-letter, no surface
apiFriction.what: The operator asks 'how many tickets did we discard this month?' and the product cannot answer. Payloads dropped at the edge (bad signature → bare 401, unparseable body, unknown channel) are not counted, not stored, and not shown anywhere. A merchant whose webhook silently 401s every ticket sees an EMPTY, CALM queue — indistinguishable from a quiet week. There is no ingest health surface at all.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness reports only the tickets that DID land; the discarded count is unknowable.

apiFriction.what: A ticket whose email matches no imported order becomes a ticket with orderId "" and a placeholder customer: no order, no wait clock, no risk, NO DRAFT. There is no 'unmatched' filter, no bucket, no count, and no way to attach it to an order after the fact. It is invisible until someone scrolls the whole queue. Every persona on a CSV path generates these (new email, second address, Apple private-relay), and they are the tickets most likely to be a real customer in trouble.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness counts tickets with an empty orderId directly from the repo.

apiFriction.where: lib/types.ts Order (no campaignId/wave/region a writer ever sets)
apiFriction.what: The operator asks 'how many messages went to the wrong campaign?' — unanswerable. Two campaigns live in one merchant record with nothing distinguishing them but a pledge date. No campaign id, no wave label, no region (region is hardcoded 'US' at import). So a reply, a band, a status page and an announcement cannot be attributed or scoped to a campaign.
apiFriction.workaround: Harness separates the two waves ONLY by pledge date, which is all the product has.
